row.notes: Sets a property value and notifies listeners on a change: rcx property P, rdx -> new value, r8d (0 at every call site; copied into the message), r9b force; returns bool. Returns 0 at once when P+0x26 bit 0 is set (0x140977b31). Reads the current value through vtable slot 0x38 of V=[P+0x58]; unless force is set, an equal first qword returns 1 with no store and no notification (0x140977b54). The compare is the only 64-bit part: every caller first checks the value type at 0x146ca5550, and most pass a 24-byte weak object handle {ptr, next, prev} and destroy it after the call, so the test is object identity, not a numeric S64 compare (a sibling for a plain qword is 0x141b85c40). Under P+0x60 bit 1 it calls 0x1442bc5b0 before the store and 0x1442bc390 after it. With listeners (P+0x40 != P+0x48) the old value is copied into a stack arena allocator (vtable 0x14565f2b0, named "unknown", 0x200-byte inline buffer). The new value is stored through V slot 0x40 (0x140977cba). When the value type is the float type at 0x146129be0, a NaN is replaced by the old value and the call returns 0 with no post hook and no notification (0x140977def), or by 1.0f when there is no non-NaN old value. Then a 0x40-byte message at rsp+0x20 (vtable 0x14565f3d0; +8 r8d, +0x10 P+8, +0x30 the old-value copy or null, +0x38 V) goes to 0x1442bc760 (0x140977dbb), which calls the 24-byte listener entries at P+0x40..+0x48 in reverse order behind a re-entrancy bit at P+0x60 bit 0. Returns 1. Callers: census steam 0x977b20, e.g. Game_Game_SetCurrentGameMode. Int32 twin = Ne_Property_SetS32IfChanged (0x140972de0).
